successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: 'After the last count died in 1497, Armagnac was united temporarily with the crown'

ledger.x: 1206: the County of Armagnac, in Gascony, is the earliest year of Cliopatria's shape.
1256: Géraud V of Fezensaguet is confirmed as Count of Armagnac, rejoining the lines after the elder branch failed in 1245; 'at his death (1285) the two counties were separated anew' (footnote 3).
1360: Armagnac is ceded to England by the Treaty of Brétigny.
1369: the count appeals to the French king and Armagnac returns to French allegiance.
1375: Cliopatria's shape grows to include the county of Rodez.
1375: the viscounties of Lomagne and Auvillars join, in Cliopatria's shape.
1375: Cliopatria's shape also holds the Lot (Quercy), which no page opened gives to Armagnac.
1385: Cliopatria's shape loses Lot and most of Tarn-et-Garonne (Quercy and Lomagne).
1385: Cliopatria's shape gains Hautes-Pyrénées cells (Bigorre), for which no page opened gives a date or a counterpart.
1407: the Hautes-Pyrénées cells leave Cliopatria's shape.
1412: Bernard VII becomes Count of Comminges.

1418: Bernard VII is killed ('On 12 June 1418, he was one of the first victims of the massacres') and Comminges leaves Armagnac, a bridge: the page does not say what became of Comminges; Cliopatria's 1422 shape lacks it.
1473: Louis XI controls the county and creates the Seneschalcy of Armagnac: 'In 1473, following the control of the county by Louis XI, the Seneschalcy of Armagnac was created.'
1497: the last count dies and Armagnac is united with the crown.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Armagnac was ceded to England in 1360, the count appealed to Charles V in 1369 and the French reconquest followed ('By 1378, under King Charles V the Wise' most ceded lands were retaken); the war ended at Castillon on 17 July 1453.

wars.name: Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War
wars.outcome: 'The two factions engaged in a bloody civil war that ended in 1435' (Armagnac page); Bernard VII, the Armagnac leader, was killed in the Burgundian massacre of Paris on 12 June 1418; the Treaty of Arras (1435) ended it.

wars.name: Siege of Lectoure
wars.outcome: Jean V was killed by the king's soldiers in Lectoure under siege in 1473 and Louis XI controlled the county; the Seneschalcy of Armagnac was created.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the Brétigny cession of 1360 names regions, not lines.
